Title: Retrieve an existing order using its string order ID and verify the response contains the correct order details with updated photo fields
Section: Order Management - Order Retrieval by String ID
Preconditions: An order with orderId '1-20231001-0001' exists in the system with customer photo and measurement cloth photo
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/1-20231001-0001 with no request body.
2. Observe the response status and body.
Expected Result: HTTP 200 OK response with a JSON body containing: {"status": "success", "message": "Order retrieved successfully", "data": {"orderId": "1-20231001-0001", "customerName": "<customer name>", "customerPhoto": "<valid photo URL>", "measurementClothPhoto": "<valid photo URL>", "items": [{"measurementGroups": [{"clothPhoto": "<valid photo URL>", "patternClothPhoto": "<valid photo URL>"}]}]}}

Title: Verify that order retrieval by orderId does not expose internal database IDs or sensitive system details
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001' and internal database ID 1001. The tester has valid authentication to access the order.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001 with valid authentication headers.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing 'status: success'. The response includes the order details with the 'orderId' field set to '50-20231001-0001' but does not expose the internal database ID (e.g., 1001) in any field or meta information.

Title: Verify that order retrieval by a non-existent orderId returns a generic error message without exposing system details
Preconditions: No order exists with orderId '99-20231001-9999'. The tester has valid authentication.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/99-20231001-9999 with valid authentication headers.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 404 (Not Found) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Order not found with orderId: 99-20231001-9999', and no sensitive system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that order retrieval by orderId rejects injection attempts via path traversal or special characters
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001'. The tester has valid authentication.
Steps:
1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001/../ with valid authentication headers.
2. Send a GET request to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001%27 with valid authentication headers.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) or 404 (Not Found) for both requests and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Invalid orderId', and no sensitive system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors).

Title: Verify that order creation with photo URLs enforces proper input validation to prevent injection or path traversal
Preconditions: The tester has valid authentication and authorization to create an order.
Steps: 1. Send a POST request to /api/orders with the payload in testData, including malicious photo URLs.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 400 (Bad Request) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Invalid photo URL', and no sensitive system details (e.g., stack traces, database errors). No order is created.

Title: Verify that order update with photo URLs enforces proper input validation to prevent injection or path traversal
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001'. The tester has valid authentication and authorization to update the order.

Title: Verify that order retrieval by orderId does not expose sensitive photo URLs to unauthorized users
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001' and contains photo URLs (e.g., customerPhoto, measurementClothPhoto). The tester does not have authorization to access the order.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001 without valid authentication or with insufficient permissions.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 403 (Forbidden) or 404 (Not Found) and a response body containing a generic error message (e.g., 'Access denied' or 'Order not found'). No photo URLs or order details are exposed.

Title: Verify that order retrieval by orderId exposes photo URLs only to authorized users
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001' and contains photo URLs (e.g., customerPhoto, measurementClothPhoto). The tester has valid authentication and authorization to access the order.
Steps: 1. Send a GET request to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001 with valid authentication headers.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) and a response body containing 'status: success'. The response includes the order details with the 'customerPhoto', 'measurementClothPhoto', 'clothPhoto', and 'patternClothPhoto' fields populated with valid URLs. No sensitive system details are exposed.

Title: Verify that order retrieval by orderId enforces rate limiting to prevent abuse
Preconditions: An order exists with orderId '50-20231001-0001'. The tester has valid authentication.
Steps: 1. Send 10 GET requests to /api/orders/50-20231001-0001 in rapid succession with valid authentication headers.
Expected Result: The API responds with HTTP status 200 (OK) for the first few requests, then starts responding with HTTP status 429 (Too Many Requests) and a response body containing 'status: error', 'message: Too many requests. Please try again later.', and no sensitive system details.
